''Iresine persica'' Burm.f. |synonyms_ref = [http://www.tropicos.org/Name/1100377?tab=synonyms ''Aerva javanica'' at Tropicos] }} '''''Aerva javanica''''', the '''kapok bush''' or '''desert cotton''', is a species of [[plant]] in the family [[Amaranthaceae]]. It has a native distribution incorporating much of Africa (including Madagascar), and the south-west and south of Asia, and it has become adventitious in northern Australia.{{GRIN | access-date = 10 January 2018}}{{Cite web|url=http://florabase.dpaw.wa.gov.au/browse/profile/2646|title=Aerva javanica (Burm.f.) Schult. Kapok Bush|date=14 August 2007|website=FloraBase|publisher=Western Australian Herbarium|access-date=27 January 2017}} ==Description== [[File:Aerva_javanica_Pilbara.jpg|left|thumb|''Aerva javanica'' (Burm.f.) Schult. in the Pilbara, Western Australia]] The plant is herbaceous, multi-stemmed and soft-wooded and bears broad leaves; it often has an erect habit and grows to a height of about {{convert|1.6|m}}. In Western Australia it tends to grow in sandy soils especially along drainage lines. It flowers between January and October.{{FloraBase|name= ''Aerva javanica'' (Burm.f.) Schult.|id=2646}} Diplospory, a type of [[Agamospermy]], occurs during the development of female gametophyte in the ovule and hence reduction division does not take place in the Megaspore mother cell. The diploid [[Egg cell|egg]] is unfertilized and forms the [[embryo]]. Hence daughter plants are exact clones of the mother. The species uses [[C4 carbon fixation|{{C4}} carbon fixation]].{{cite journal |last1=Sage |first1=R.F. |last2=Sage |first2=T.L. |last3=Pearcy |first3=R.W. |last4=Borsch |first4=T. |title=The taxonomic distribution of {{C4}} photosynthesis in Amaranthaceae sensu stricto|journal=American Journal of Botany |volume=94 |issue=12 |year=2007 |pages=1992–2003 |issn=0002-9122 |doi=10.3732/ajb.94.12.1992 |pmid=21636394}} {{open access}} It is [[dioecious]], meaning male and female flowers are produced on separate individuals.{{cite journal|doi=10.17660/ActaHortic.2017.1155.88|title=Establishment of vitroplants from female flowers of ''Aerva javanica'' (Burm. F) Juss ex Schult|year=2017|last1=Chabane|first1=D.|last2=Mouhoub|first2=F.|journal=Acta Horticulturae|issue=1155|pages=607–612}} ==Uses== This [[herb]] is deep rooted, and is used as soil binder in [[desert reclamation]].L R Burdak (1982): Recent advances in desert afforestation, Dehradun, p. 66 It is used for fuel and for fodder for goats. In traditional medicine the seeds are believed to cure headaches.{{citation needed|date=September 2017}} A gargle is made from the plant to try to treat toothache.{{cite journal |author1=Muhammad Qasim Samejo |author2=Shahabuddin Memon |author3=Muhammad Iqbal Bhanger |author4=Khalid Mohammed Khan |year=2011 |title=Chemical Compositions of the Essential oil of ''Aerva javanica'' Leaves and Stems |journal=Pak. J. Anal. Environ. Chem |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=48–52 |issn=1996-918X }} The plant has naturalised in northern regions of Australia, as an alien introduction, and is cultivated and utilised by the [[indigenous peoples]] of some countries. The thick, white inflorescences have traditionally been harvested in [[Arabia]] for stuffing cushions and saddle pads.M.A. Zahran & A.J. Willis, ''The Vegetation of Egypt'', Hong Kong 1992, pp. 187–188 {{ISBN|978-0-412-31510-7}}James P. Mandaville, ''Bedouin Ethnobotany - Plant Concepts and Uses in a Desert Pastoral World'', University of Arizona Press 2011, [https://books.google.com/books?id=rRZm5-e486wC&dq=bedouin+ethnobotany+aerva+javanica&pg=PA154 p. 154], ({{ISBN|978-0-8165-2900-1}}) Today, the soft fibres are still used as [[Ceiba pentandra|kapok]] for pillows. It is called Bilhangga in the languages of the [[Yindjibarndi]] and [[Ngarluma]] people, the English term is Kapok Bush.{{Cite book|title=Wanggalili; Yinjibarndi and Ngarluma Plants|author =Burndud|publisher= Juluwarlu Aboriginal Corporation |year=1990|page = 17}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.flowersinisrael.com/Aervajavanica_page.htm Aerva javanica] Flowers in Israel {{WestAfricanPlants|Aerva javanica}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q3695262}} [[Category:Aerva|javanica]] [[Category:Flora of Africa]] [[Category:Flora of Western Asia]] [[Category:Flora of the Indian subcontinent]] [[Category:Flora of the Arabian Peninsula]] [[Category:Herbs]] [[Category:Dioecious plants]] [[Category:Taxa named by Nicolaas Laurens Burman]] [[Category:Drought-tolerant plants]]
